newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens vs dlr amid jittery trade.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens vs dlr amid jittery trade.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling, already on a weakening spree, made further losses against the dollar on Wednesday, in nervous trade, signalling what forex dealers said could be the beginning of pre-election jitters.
Against the dollar, Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 55.87 from Tuesday's mean of 55.35 while against the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean of 94.26 from 93.34.
Dealers said strong demand from foreign investors buying dollars in anticipation of a weakening shilling was the main reason for the shilling's steady losses against the dollar.

"The market is uncertain. Everyone is keeping wide spreads -- up to 50 cents," one dealer said. "Any dollars coming into the market are being snapped up immediately. It's like going down a sinking hole," he added.
Reports of violence, unrest and heightening political tension, if prolonged, could weaken Kenya's currency even further, market analysts said.

"Everyone understands that this could be a one-off stand. But a prolonged period of political uncertainty would in the medium term affect the shilling," John Munge, Managing Director of leading brokerage house Shah, Munge & Partners told Reuters.
One analyst said the shilling would be affected by whatever decision investors made -- for the long term, especially if they decided they would hold out until election after elections.
Kenya's presidential and parliamentary elections are scheduled for later this year.
Meanwhile the money market eased marginally. Overnight rates were quoted at between 17 and 22 percent from 23 percent on Tuesday.
